newsitem.title: UK: Seasonal calm descends upon Europe's mkts.
newsitem.headline: Seasonal calm descends upon Europe's mkts.

text.p: London and French shares were little changed and the dollar was steady in thin trade on Tuesday with many traders planning to finish early for the Christmas holiday and German markets closed. In London, shares opened a touch easier, but were 5.2 points firmer by 1000 GMT, dealers said. Gilts were flat in early dealings, while the Dow, up about 20 points when London markets closed, ended with just a 4.62 point gain last night at 6,489.02. London stocks hit a closing peak for the second session running on Monday.

"There's not enough impetus today to move much higher, but I don't see why we wouldn't end the day a bit better," said one dealer. "Most institutions aren't in the market and those that are can't afford to sell."

In an interview with France's Le Figaro newspaper, Bank of England governor Eddie George said he did not rule out a British rate rise before the election, which must be held by mid-May, and dealers said that might dampen enthusiasm for gilts.
However, gilts weathered yesterday's release of the October 30 monetary minutes between George and Chancellor Kenneth Clarke, interpreted by some analysts as signalling a forthcoming rate rise.
The London Stock Exchange is scheduled to close at 1230 GMT.

French shares opened with narrow gains across the board, with operators adding stocks on the first day of the new account, traders said. But prices then dipped into the minus column once the initial buying was absorbed.
There was little appetite for taking risks ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday and London closing at midday. Fund managers were happy to lock in the year's 25 percent rise.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 6.51 points or 0.28 percent at 2,293.95 at 0915 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,291 from 2,296 on Monday's close.
Volume was around 276 million francs.
The dollar was steady against the mark in Europe as the market ground to a halt on Christmas Eve with some centres, including Germany, already closed for the break.
Traders in London were looking for a short day's trading and the market here will effectively finish business soon after midsession, dealers said.
The dollar was a touch firmer against the yen at 114.37. Japan's index of leading indicators stood at 83.3 in October, above the so-called boom-or-bust level of 50 for the second consecutive month.
A figure above 50 is generally taken as suggesting that the economy will expand in the coming months. This could lead to higher Japanese interest rates.
Tokyo stocks fell sharply to a fresh 12-month low as the market fretted over the outlook for the Japanese economy.
The market's key Nikkei average fell as investors turned increasingly gloomy, despite optimistic comments from government officials about Japan's economic recovery.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5550 marks and 114.37 yen compared with 1.5555 marks and 114.12 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 5.2 points at 4,092.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share was down 3.44 at 2,284.00
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was closed on Tuesday for the Christmas holiday. The index fell 8.88 points on Monday to 2,845.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $369.00 compared with $368.85 an ounce in late trade on Monday.
